lesson.title: The Extended Clan
lesson.subtitle: Großvater, Oma, Onkel, Enkel — compounds, nursery words and the ankle surprise

hook.title: Compounds, Loans and One Ankle
hook.content: The extended family shows all three ways German builds kin vocabulary. Compounds from parts you own: Großvater (big-father), Großmutter (big-mother), Großeltern (the big-elders). Shared Romance loans: Onkel and Tante came from French oncle/tante — the same loans English took, and Cousin/Cousine likewise. Nursery words: Oma and Opa are German inventions with no English relatives — honest memorize words. And one fossil: Enkel, grandchild, is the same ancient word as ANKLE — both mean 'bender', the ankle's joint becoming the family's 'little bender', the one a generation below. Even Geschwister, siblings, is built: ge- + Schwester, 'sister-hood' for brothers and sisters alike.

footnotes.title: Schwieger-: the Quiet In-Law Prefix
footnotes.content: Schwiegermutter (mother-in-law) hides Schwieger, an old word for 'affinity by marriage' with no English cousin — but its second half is Mutter, the unchanged twin. German in-law words are compounds wearing one unknown bead on a familiar string.

pattern.title: The Clan in Sentences
pattern.content: Mein Großvater liest die Zeitung. Meine Großmutter backt einen Kuchen (the baker verb at work). Meine Tante schenkt mir ein Buch. Ich habe zwei Geschwister — plural counting like English siblings. Der Enkel besucht seinen Großvater. Note the pattern: kin nouns for men take der/mein, for women die/meine, and the compounds follow their HEAD noun — Großmutter is die because Mutter is. Family gatherings are grammar drills: Meine Familie ist groß. — with Geschwister, Eltern, Cousin und Cousine all pulling their genders behind them.
pattern.linguist_note: Enkel and ankle both descend from Proto-Germanic *ankulaz, 'that which bends'. English kept the body-part sense; German's word bent socially — the grandchild as the family's small joint, linking the generations like an ankle links foot and leg.

exercises.target_answer: der Großvater, die Großmutter, der Onkel, die Tante, der Enkel
exercises.explanation: Compounds (Groß+vater), shared French loans (Onkel, Tante) and one fossil (Enkel ↔ ankle) — the clan in five words.
ge- collects a group around one noun: one Schwester, but Geschwister for the whole set of brothers and sisters.

exercises.prompt: Enkel shares its ancient root with which English body word?
exercises.explanation: Both words mean 'the bender': English kept the joint, German bent the word toward the youngest generation.

exercises.prompt: Which nursery word is German for grandma (no English twin — honest memorize; three letters)?
exercises.meaning: Oma = grandma (a nursery coinage, cognate only with Dutch)
exercises.explanation: Oma and Opa are German nursery inventions — the honest no-cognate words of the family tree.

exercises.prompt: Say in German: "Meine Oma ist sehr alt = my grandma is very old"
exercises.meaning: Meine Oma ist sehr alt = my grandma is very old

vocab_hints.note: the intensifier from earlier trail lessons

exercises.explanation: die Oma → meine Oma: the feminine possessor — and alt closes the loop with Eltern, 'the elder ones', from lesson 5091.
exercises.idea: Meine Oma ist sehr alt = my grandma is very old
idea_parts: = my grandma is very old (verb in position 2)
cues: Start with "Meine" and anchor "Oma" in position 2.

summary.outcome: Talk about the extended family using compounds, loans and nursery words with correct genders.

use_example.german: Meine Großeltern wohnen bei uns, und meine Cousine kommt oft.
use_example.english: My grandparents live with us, and my (female) cousin visits often.

summary.takeaway: Großvater = compound, Onkel/Tante = shared French loans, Oma/Opa = honest memorize, Enkel ↔ ankle, Geschwister = ge- + Schwester.
summary.curiosity_teaser: The clan branch ends here — the map's remaining sprigs and the capstone reading still wait.

großvater.etymology_derivation: groß (big) + Vater; the Vater root is father via Verner's law, not V→B. [wiktionary]

großmutter.context_translation: My grandmother is baking a cake.
großmutter.etymology_derivation: groß (big) + Mutter; Mutter is the unchanged twin of English mother. [wiktionary]

oma.context_phrase: Meine Oma wohnt auf dem Land.
oma.context_translation: My grandma lives in the countryside.
oma.etymology_derivation: Nursery word, cognate only with Dutch oma; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

opa.etymology_derivation: Nursery word, cognate only with Dutch opa; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

onkel.context_phrase: Mein Onkel kommt morgen zu Besuch.
onkel.context_translation: My uncle is coming to visit tomorrow.
onkel.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French oncle — the same French/Latin source as English uncle. [wiktionary]

tante.context_phrase: Meine Tante schenkt mir ein Buch.
tante.context_translation: My aunt is giving me a book.
tante.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from French tante; English aunt descends from the related Old French form. [wiktionary]

geschwister.etymology_derivation: ge- + Schwester — built on the same root as English sister (*swestēr). [wiktionary]

enkel.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *ankulaz 'ankle' — the same root as English ankle, meaning shifted to 'grandchild'. [wiktionary]

familie.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Latin familia — the same Latin source as English family. [wiktionary]

tschüss.etymology_derivation: CONFIRMED: Low German adjüs, from Dutch adjuus, from French adieu / Spanish adiós — 'to God' worn down to bye. [wiktionary]

kakao.etymology_derivation: Kakao — borrowed from Spanish cacao, from Classical Nahuatl cacahuatl (cacao bean); English cocoa and cacao share the same Nahuatl source. [wiktionary]

ordentlich.etymology_derivation: From ordnen 'to put in order' + -lich; Ordnung 'order' is the same family. [wiktionary]

biene.etymology_derivation: From Middle High German bine, from Old High German bini, from Proto-West Germanic *bini. English bee is the cognate from the same bee-root. [wiktionary]

schauspieler.context_phrase: Der Schauspieler steht auf der Bühne.
schauspieler.context_translation: The actor stands on the stage.
schauspieler.etymology_derivation: Schauspiel + -er - literally a show-player; Schau is the same old word as English show (Proto-Germanic *skawwōną, Old English sceawian). [wiktionary]

partner.context_phrase: Mein Partner und ich arbeiten zusammen.
partner.context_translation: My partner and I work together.
partner.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from English partner — the same word, reshaped to German pronunciation, with feminine Partnerin. [wiktionary]
